items.title: Add a global option to serialise/deserialise enums by name not value
items.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

There's an existing [discussion](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/discussions/2980) about this which started off as a feature request but was changed to a discussion. I think that discussion has run its course so I'd like to make a feature request which can either be progressed, or closed if the project does not want to go that way.

This feature request is for a single, global flag added to the configuration:

- Add a boolean configuration option: "serialise_enum_by_name" or similar, default False.
- If it is False: no change to serialisation / schemas.
- If it is True: serialisation / de-serialisation uses the enum name, and generated schemas contain a list of enum names.

I think this needs to be part of the core library as there have been a few suggested workarounds over time in the linked discussion, but they all rely on specific internal behaviour at the time and eventually break with newer releases.

There is some discussion in the linked issue of a non-global requirement that could be applied to specific enum instances. I'd like to explicitly exclude those from this feature request: I think that is a sufficiently different use case that if people want that it should go in its own request.





### Affected Components

- [ ] [Compatibility between releases](https://docs.pydantic.dev/changelog/)
- [x] [Data validation/parsing](https://docs.pydantic.dev/concepts/models/#basic-model-usage)
- [x] [Data serialization](https://docs.pydantic.dev/concepts/serialization/) - `.model_dump()` and `.model_dump_json()`
- [x] [JSON Schema](https://docs.pydantic.dev/concepts/json_schema/)
- [ ] [Dataclasses](https://docs.pydantic.dev/concepts/dataclasses/)
- [ ] [Model Config](https://docs.pydantic.dev/concepts/config/)
- [ ] [Field Types](https://docs.pydantic.dev/api/types/) - adding or changing a particular data type
- [ ] [Function validation decorator](https://docs.pydantic.dev/concepts/validation_decorator/)
- [ ] [Generic Models](https://docs.pydantic.dev/concepts/models/#generic-models)
- [ ] [Other Model behaviour](https://docs.pydantic.dev/concepts/models/) - `model_construct()`, pickling, private attributes, ORM mode
- [ ] [Plugins](https://docs.pydantic.dev/) and integration with other tools - mypy, FastAPI, python-devtools, Hypothesis, VS Code, PyCharm, etc.

BUG REPORT: openai.BadRequestError when using Gemini models for tool calls
============================================================

## Error Message
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'Tool call function arguments must be valid JSON.', 'type': 'invalid_request_error'}}

## Code to Reproduce
```python
from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_ext.models.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient

model = OpenAIChatCompletionClient(
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
)
agent = AssistantAgent("helper", model_client=model, tools=[my_tool])
result = await agent.run(task="What is the weather in NYC?")
```

## Environment
autogen-agentchat==0.5.6
autogen-ext==0.5.6
openai==1.82.0
Python 3.11.5

## Expected Behavior
Tool call should execute successfully with Gemini models

## Actual Behavior
Raises openai.BadRequestError with invalid JSON error for tool call arguments

## Additional Context
Occurs consistently. Tested on Ubuntu 22.04.

items.title: # SIGSEGV at shutdown (`Py_FinalizeEx` / GC): Django + pydantic-core (Python 3.12)
items.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Maybe Related: [pydantic#12867](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12867).

## Summary

When running Django’s test runner inside a Docker CI image with **`pydantic`** /
**`pydantic-core`** pins in the **2.11+** line, the **test suite reports success**, then
the **Python process segfaults during teardown** while the interpreter is shutting down
(**garbage collection** → **`Py_FinalizeEx`**).

Under **`gdb`**, the crashing thread shows **three frames inside**
**`pydantic_core/_pydantic_core.cpython-312-…so`** immediately above **`datetime_dealloc`**
in **`_datetime.cpython-312-…so`**. That matches the **shutdown / datetime /
pydantic-core** pattern discussed in **#12867** (the issue’s Python 3.11 trace includes
**`TzInfo`** / **`_Py_Dealloc`**).

We do **not** have a minimal public repro without our application code; this report
documents **versions**, **symptoms**, **`gdb`** capture, and **how we run tests** so
maintainers can compare with **#12867** and decide whether this is the same root cause on
**Python 3.12**.

---

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| OS / image | Rocky Linux 9–style container (`test-django` in our repo) |
| Python | **3.12** |
| Packages (repro) | **`pydantic==2.13.2`**, **`pydantic-core==2.46.2`** (`pip -U` in image) |
| Runner | Django **`manage.py test`** with Postgres + Redis (Compose) |
| Baseline (stable in our runs) | **`pydantic==2.10.6`**, **`pydantic-core==2.27.2`** |

---

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** After tests finish, the process exits with code **0** and the interpreter
shuts down cleanly.

**Actual:**

- Tests print **`OK`** and normal Django teardown (including **`Flushing redis…`**).
- Then either:
  - **`Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault`** (stderr), often **`Garbage-collecting`**
    with no Python frame; exit **139**, or
  - Under **`gdb`**: **`SIGSEGV`** with the stack below.

The failure happens **after** tests succeed, during **finalization / GC**, not during
assertions.

---

## Reproduction notes (our stack)

These steps assume our monorepo layout (`/myapp` in the container). They are **not** a
fully self-contained upstream repro; they show how we trigger the crash.

1. Start Compose (from our `docker/` dir): **`test-django`** with healthy Postgres
   and Redis.
2. Upgrade pins (example): `pip install -U 'pydantic==2.13.2'` (pulls
   **`pydantic-core==2.46.2`**).
3. Run **`manage.py test`** against a subset that imports **Pydantic `BaseModel`** (we used
   `myapp.dashboards.models.tests.test_build`).
4. Invoke **`python …/manage.py`** with the same
   **`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`** as **`./manage`** (via **`.environment`**); otherwise unrelated
   native imports fail before Django starts.

**Docker / `gdb`:**

- **`--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE`** on **`docker compose run`** so **`gdb`** can run the inferior.
- Debug with **`gdb --args /myapp/manage.py test …`**
  (interpreter + **`manage.py`**); do not run **`gdb`** on **`python`** alone.

---

## GDB stack trace (abbreviated — Python 3.12)

Fault thread (**Thread 1**). Other threads were idle OpenBLAS helpers.

```text

Fault thread is **Thread 1** (main); other threads are idle OpenBLAS workers.

```text

Interpretation: crash while **`datetime_dealloc`** runs during **`gc_collect_main`** on the **`Py_FinalizeEx`** path — **`pydantic_core`** native frames above **`datetime_dealloc`**, aligning with **`#12867`** (timezone / pydantic-core / interpreter shutdown).


**`pydantic_core`** shows **`??`** without wheel debug symbols; the signal is **native
pydantic_core → `datetime_dealloc` → finalize/GC**.

---

## Relation to #12867

**[#12867](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12867)** describes a shutdown
**`SIGSEGV`** with **`pydantic_core`** and **`datetime`** / **`TzInfo`** involvement. Our
**3.12** trace is **consistent** (pydantic_core above **`datetime_dealloc`** during
teardown). We are **not** claiming an identical root cause without upstream review.

---

## What we cannot supply yet

- A **minimal** reproducer without our Django models and imports.
- Whether **`pydantic==2.13.3`** / **`pydantic-core==2.46.3`** fixes shutdown on **this**
  path (not used in the **`gdb`** capture above).
